character.name: Septimus Bracket
character.description: A thin, anxious presence in an apron stiff with official starch, leaning on a staff with notches cut for every complaint. Septimus is a Professional Mourner, Between Engagements and is keeping in practice and will be sad about anything, on request.

npc.narrative: At alba the pioggia falls on the Sensible Pasture at the Usual Place like a verdict. Septimus Bracket waits sotto a grande nero ombrello beside the cancello, holding a piccolo card of opening hours that is, on inspection, vuoto. One pecora watches from the fence, un po' unimpressed.
npc.native: Buongiorno! Oggi sono felice, perché piove e io lavoro bene quando piove. Di solito chiedo «che succede?» e poi dico «ti capisco». E tu, come stai oggi, e che cosa pensi del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: Good morning! Today I am happy, because it is raining and I work well when it rains. Usually I ask "what is wrong?" and then I say "I understand you". And you, how are you today, and what do you think of my work?

player: Buongiorno! Anch'io sono felice oggi, perché ho trovato un nuovo lavoro. Il tuo lavoro è un po' strano, ma interessante.

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely answer! You said you are happy and gave a reason, and you shared your opinion of Septimus's work, all in correct Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you told Septimus you are happy today in good Italian.
Not yet: you still need to ask Septimus what is wrong. Don't worry, he will give you another chance to ask later.
Not yet: you still need to tell Septimus that you understand, or that you are very sorry. Septimus will ask for this again later.

openObjectives.prompt: Septimus is staring into a cup of something that went cold a good while ago. Ask Septimus what is wrong, using Italian.
Tell Septimus that you understand, or that you are very sorry, using Italian.

npc.narrative: The alba is grigia, and Septimus lowers his nero ombrello like a man who has been sad in worse weather. Across the strada, the guanti of his cugino hang from a chiodo, better made than his own. He does not look at them, which takes pratica and a certain amount of fango.
npc.native: Un nuovo lavoro, che bello! Io invece sono un po' triste, perché oggi non ho nessun funerale. La gente guarda la mia faccia e chiede: «Che succede?», e poi dice: «Ti capisco». E tu, che lavoro fai adesso, e come sono i tuoi primi giorni?
npc.translation: A new job, how nice! I, on the other hand, am a little sad, because today I have no funeral. People look at my face and ask: "What is wrong?", and then say: "I understand you." And you, what job do you do now, and how are your first days?

player: Lavoro in una biblioteca, i primi giorni sono tranquilli. Ma tu, che succede? Sembri triste davvero.

verdict.overallFeedback: Nice answer: you told Septimus about your work in the library and asked him what is wrong, all in good Italian. Next, try comforting him.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: you asked Septimus what is wrong with "Che succede?".
Not yet: tell Septimus that you understand, or that you are very sorry. We will ask for this again soon.

openObjectives.prompt: Tell Septimus that you understand, or that you are very sorry, using Italian.

npc.narrative: At dawn the cielo is perfectly clear, which Septimus accepts like a man refused a refund. He turns his black cappello in his hands, slowly, as if it were a ledger nobody has asked to see. Beside him a panchina waits, with room for two and a poor opinion of both.
npc.native: Sì, sono triste davvero, grazie! Oggi non c'è nessun funerale, e mio cugino ha tre funerali. Quando un amico è triste, io dico: «Ti capisco». E tu, che cosa dici a un uomo triste come me, e che libri ci sono nella tua biblioteca?
npc.translation: Yes, I am truly sad, thank you! Today there is no funeral, and my cousin has three funerals. When a friend is sad, I say: "I understand you." And you, what do you say to a sad man like me, and what books are there in your library?

player: Mi dispiace molto, Septimus. Ti capisco, anche io sono geloso di mio fratello a volte. Nella biblioteca ci sono molti libri di cucina.

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely answer! You comforted Septimus with kind words, shared a feeling of your own and told him about the books in your library, all in clear Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: You told Septimus you understand and that you are sorry, in good Italian.

npc.narrative: Il sole rises over the colline, and the rain has gone, which Septimus takes personally. He folds a nero fazzoletto with great care and looks at you like un uomo who has been understood before colazione. Somewhere a campana rings, per nessuno in particular.
npc.native: Grazie, amico mio, ora sono meno triste! «Ti capisco» è una frase bella, e tu la dici bene. Mio cugino è più bravo di me, ma io sono più triste di lui. Che cosa cucini con i libri di cucina, e com'è tuo fratello?
npc.translation: Thank you, my friend, now I am less sad! "I understand you" is a lovely phrase, and you say it well. My cousin is better than me, but I am sadder than him. What do you cook with the cookbooks, and what is your brother like?

player: Mio fratello è molto simpatico ma fa sempre tutto meglio di me, che noia! Io cucino la pasta, sempre. E tu, cosa fai per essere felice quando non c'è un funerale?

npc.narrative: The cielo is clear at dawn, which Septimus takes as a personal insult. He sits on a low muro, cappello on his ginocchio, and practises a sospiro with the calm of a man in perfetta forma. A gatto on the tetto is not impressed.
npc.native: La pasta, sempre? È una vita onesta! Quando non c'è un funerale, io sono triste per un amico, perché devo stare in forma. Mio cugino è triste meglio di me, ma io ho un buon orario. Chiedimi pure del mio lavoro, se vuoi; e dimmi, come cucini la pasta?
npc.translation: Pasta, always? That is an honest life! When there is no funeral, I am sad for a friend, because I have to keep in shape. My cousin is sad better than I am, but I have good hours. Ask me about my work, if you like; and tell me, how do you cook the pasta?

player: Con pomodoro e basilico, niente di speciale. Ma dimmi, come ti senti quando sei triste per lavoro? È vero o è finto?

npc.narrative: The sky is perfectly clear, which Septimus accepts as a personal remark. He sits on a **panchina** outside the **cimitero**, holding his black hat the way other men hold a **piatto** of soup. He considers your question for a long moment, like a man reading a notice that has not yet been written.
npc.native: Pomodoro e basilico: è una pasta buona! Quando sono triste per lavoro, è un po' vero e un po' finto. La tristezza è vera, ma il mio orario è finto, perché nessuno lo conosce. Mio cugino è più bravo di me, ovviamente. Chiedimi pure di più sul mio lavoro; e tu, che cosa fai la sera dopo la biblioteca?
npc.translation: Tomato and basil: that is a good pasta! When I am sad for work, it is a little true and a little fake. The sadness is true, but my timetable is fake, because nobody knows it. My cousin is better than me, obviously. Do ask me more about my work; and you, what do you do in the evening after the library?
